A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TABREX and TABREX-BENCH. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-ranking correlations, perturbation-robustness experiments, text-to-table evaluation, and model–prompt analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original extraction-quality and score-sensitivity results using human-authored knowledge graphs.

M1.justification: The Text2Graph, rule-based Table2Graph, alignment, and scoring procedures remain unchanged, as do their prompts and weights. Appendix C tests alternative extractors and matching criteria without documenting a revision to the proposed TABREX pipeline.

E1.justification: The six source datasets, perturbation scenarios, and text-to-table coverage are retained. The new validation uses five summaries from each existing domain; its gold annotations and component checks do not establish expanded domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. New Appendix C adds Qwen3.5-27B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B as extractor comparators alongside the default GPT-5-nano, with human-authored graphs providing the control.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a substantial component-validation protocol: 30 stratified summaries, 364 manually authored gold triples, four matching criteria, micro- and macro-averaged metrics, and controlled graph-source substitutions with table graphs and scoring fixed. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct extraction-quality audit, coverage and faithfulness diagnostics, comparison of LLM and embedding-based matching, and sensitivity of final scores to gold versus extracted graphs. These analyses investigate error propagation through a central component that v1 did not directly validate.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports p-values for Spearman correlations with gold-graph scores. The four pipeline executions per sample represent different graph-source conditions, not repeated seeds; no new confidence intervals or stochastic-run uncertainty estimates are reported.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated results are unchanged. Tables 6–8 add substantive extraction and score-stability findings, including gold-score Spearman correlations of 0.822, 0.711, and 0.830 for GPT-5-nano, Qwen, and Gemma. New mean scores are 39.43, 40.04, and 39.98 versus 39.71 using gold graphs.

T1.justification: Table 7 adds operational definitions of entity coverage, using at least 80% token overlap, and faithfulness, using source-supported extracted objects. These are limited metric-definition additions; the TABREX penalty equations and worked derivation remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reference-less evaluation, the six-domain benchmark, human alignment, robustness, and explainable diagnostics. The new appendix supplies supporting evidence without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly attributes weak exact matching to paraphrasing, interprets agreement between semantic and embedding matchers as ruling out circularity, and argues that extractor choice is well controlled. These extend the reliability interpretation; the main limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the embedding checkpoint, matching thresholds, and alignment-cache keys for the new validation. Its Maintenance and Adoption Plan adds MIT licensing, stated dataset hosting and versioning, and maintenance arrangements. v1 already supplied the same code link, prompts, weights, and hardware information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. The altered InternVL3.5 citation and malformed bibliography entry refer to the same work, rather than adding or replacing a reference.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and author/contact edits, reorders the existing appendices, updates cross-references, and adds maintenance and acknowledgment sections. Most existing prose is retained. It also introduces typographical defects, including rendering the former range 45–53 as 4553 and corrupting the InternVL citation.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8, relocates Table 3 and Figure 4, and expands Prompt A from a single-column box to a full-width box. Existing figures retain their content, and the overall two-column design remains substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new gold-graph validation provides useful evidence about a previously untested dependency, while the implementation and maintenance disclosures improve reproducibility information. The gain is limited: only 30 summaries are checked, and matcher agreement does not establish that circularity is ruled out. New range and citation formatting errors also reduce clarity. Overall, the added evidence supports a modest improvement.
